cars.variant: Three-door Turbo S — original January 1986 Japan five-speed reference
cars.specification_market: Original 8 January 1986 Japanese Turbo S three-door with five-speed manual. Factory native PS and kg-m remain unconverted; the 2019 publisher’s republication of its period test identifies the manual reference and peak speeds. No later 110 PS tune, ordinary Si engine/weight, TEMS standard-fit claim, automatic specification, production total or 0–400 m-to-0–100 km/h substitution is imported.
cars.summary: The first turbo Starlet established the compact, forceful performance identity that preceded the later GT Turbo and Glanza. Its intercooled engine offered driver-selectable boost modes. Motor Magazine’s retrospective draws on its own period test and recognises the EP71 as a Japanese boys-racer landmark, while describing demanding handling that required skill to manage. This original turbo generation merits one entry.

cars.generation: N15 / JN15 Pulsar high-performance production-road hatchback family
cars.variant: VZ-R N1 — September 1997 Japan standard road-equipment reference
cars.specification_market: September 1997 Autech/Nissan brochure, both pages visually read. Selects the standard road-equipped N1, not the separately listed race-base deletions. Native PS/torque units retained. The original viscous LSD is not a later helical substitution. Large roof spoiler and side stripes are options, not universal equipment. The announced combined Pulsar/Lucino allocation is not proved production, and rebadges, Version II and ordinary VZ-R add no extra count.
cars.summary: Autech’s Pulsar VZ-R N1 represents the high-revving engineering of Japan’s 1990s performance hatchbacks. Its 1596 cc SR16VE combined switchable valve timing and lift with dedicated cylinder-head, intake and exhaust work to produce 200 PS. Further balancing and port finishing distinguish the N1 programme. That specific engine development, rather than the announced limited allocation alone, justifies its place.

cars.generation: Original M112S Storia X4 production-road motorsport-base hatchback family
cars.variant: X4 M112S-GMNZ — original April 1998 Japan retail programme
cars.specification_market: Original 10 April 1998 Japanese retail X4 M112S-GMNZ, sold as a small passenger car and motorsport base with road equipment. Road specification is from the factory release; competition results establish heritage only. No later Boon X4, ordinary 1.0/1.3-litre Sirion Rally, unsupported 120 PS/boost figure, regulatory-capacity formula or race tune is transferred.
cars.summary: The Storia X4 gave a small road hatch an unusually focused factory motorsport package: a 713 cc twin-cam turbo four with forged pistons and crankshaft, full-time four-wheel drive and front and rear limited-slip differentials. A close-ratio manual and reinforced chassis completed the package. This specialised engineering, backed by an actual M112S competition record, distinguishes it from an ordinary Storia or Sirion.

facts.title: Documented competition heritage
facts.explanation: JAF records an M112S Storia winning the A1 class at round two of the 2000 All-Japan Dirt Trial Championship. This establishes actual competition success for the programme; the race car’s modifications are not the retail X4 specification.
